# AI Interfaces

> Case studies and measurements on user interfaces designed, built, changed or checked with AI:
> what was measured, against whom, what worked and what failed.

**Unofficial. No company named here endorses or is affiliated with this project.** Company and
product names describe the subject of each case only. Summaries are in our own words and link to
their primary sources.

<!-- disclosure: generated by scripts/build.mjs -->
Disclosure: the cases and lessons are drafted by Claude, an Anthropic model, and reviewed by the maintainer. At least 5 of the 10 cases involve Claude models or Claude Code, as builders, judges or models under test (studio-go, Agentic audit, Anthropic harness, ArtifactsBench, UW heuristic review); 1 leaves the models unstated. Anthropic is the author or the subject of one case: Anthropic adds a planner and a Playwright grading agent to Claude app builds; by the engineer's account the game maker works where a solo run broke, at over 20x the cost. One case is the maintainer's own project (studio-go, marked maintainer-own): never independent evidence, and never counted toward a lesson's strength.

## What it does

<!-- contents: generated by scripts/build.mjs -->
Now: 10 cases (UCI code study, Brazil heuristic review, UW heuristic review, ArtifactsBench, UW walkthrough, Anthropic harness, GitHub a11y agent, Concordia repair, Agentic audit, studio-go), 49 lessons on 5 aspect pages, and a checklist of 10 questions.
<!-- /contents -->

- **Cases** ([cases/](cases/), listed in [index.md](index.md)): one file per piece of work where AI
  designed, built, changed or checked an interface: a team's story, a benchmark or a study. Each
  says what AI, rule-based tools and people did, what was measured and against whom (real users or
  experts, an automated checker, a model judge), the numbers with their basis, and what went wrong.
- **Lessons** ([lessons/](lessons/)): what the cases teach, by aspect. Every lesson says whether it
  depends on model ability and what checked its evidence: people, a checker, a model, or only the
  author's account.
- **Checklist** ([checklist.md](checklist.md)): only what an agent can measure on a project before
  and after a change (jobs in screens and clicks, accessibility violations, contrast pairs,
  controls and consistency). It never asks for a judgement of taste.
- **For agents** ([llms.txt](llms.txt)): how to use the collection, reading only what a task needs.

The collection measures; it never says which look is better: taste stays with a person.
[log.md](log.md) records what each update covered.

## What it covers today and what it does not

- **Covered:** accessibility (what checkers, model fixes and audit agents catch and miss), model
  judges and heuristic reviews compared with experts, simulated users compared with people, counting
  what jobs cost in screens and clicks, and the loops agents build and check interfaces in.
- **Not yet:** visual design, layout and component consistency. The checklist counts consistency,
  but only the maintainer's own project reports such counts.
- **Known gaps:** no measured study of how alike AI-made designs are (sameness), no benchmark that
  compares model generations on the same interface tasks, and no real redesign reported with
  numbers apart from the maintainer's own.

## Try it

Open your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) in your project and pick a route. Step 1
only reads your project and changes nothing: you get measurements and numbered proposals, each
with a one-word recommendation (do, later or skip) and a reason, and you choose. No proposal says
which look is better. Run step 1 in a fresh session. The prompts for step 2 (apply), step 3
(revisit later) and sharing a field report are in [docs/try-it.md](docs/try-it.md).

### Before an interface change

Run the checklist on the project whose interface you are about to change with AI. It counts what
an agent can measure and how your agents check their work, with a baseline for every count so the
same counts can be taken after the change. Paste:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/llms.txt and follow it. Run the checklist on this project: measure every question with its check, on a running page where the check needs one and I allow it, else by its static route marked "static"; do not judge from memory or from how the interface looks. Report in the checklist's report format: each answer with its measurement, a baseline for every count, and the cases behind each gap. Give each proposal a recommendation of exactly one word, do, later or skip, with a reason. Change nothing.
```

### Learning from the lessons

Compare how agents build, change and check interfaces in your project with what these cases
taught. Lessons whose evidence people confirmed ("Checked against people: yes") travel furthest;
each is still judged by its own words. Paste:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/llms.txt and follow its route for learning from the lessons, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/docs/applying-lessons.md. Compare the lessons with how this project's agents build, change and check its interface today; measure from the repository and its history, do not judge from memory or from how the interface looks. Report in that page's report format: numbered proposals, each with the lesson ID, what the project does now with its measurement, the change, its cost, its baseline and the check that would prove it. Give each proposal a recommendation of exactly one word, do, later or skip, with a reason. Change nothing.
```

## Status

Live: the first ten cases, the lessons they support and the checklist, with two routes to apply
them ("Try it" above), `llms.txt` for agents and the field-report form. The update log says what
each update changed; a release is tagged monthly.

## Contributing

Corrections are welcome: a wrong number, a broken link, a summary that misreads its source. Open
an issue; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). [docs/format.md](docs/format.md) describes the case
format and the rules every file follows.
